The fluorescent lights of the 42nd floor hummed with the same energy as the panic rising in Arthur’s chest. It was Bring Your Pet to Work Day, and Arthur had made a catastrophic error in judgment. He had brought Barnaby, a African Grey Parrot with a vocabulary that exceeded his own and a memory that rivaled a hard drive.

Barnaby was perched on the edge of Arthur’s monitor, preening a feather with an air of smug indifference. Arthur, meanwhile, was sweating through his shirt, staring at the bird as if it were a ticking time bomb wrapped in colorful feathers.

"Good morning, Arthur," Barnaby squawked, his voice a perfect, terrifying clone of the CEO, Mr. Henderson. "The quarterly earnings are a disaster. We’re cooking the books. Also, I stole the stapler."

Arthur froze. His hand hovered over the phone, which was currently ringing. It was the CFO.

"Hello?" Arthur squeaked, his voice an octave higher than usual.

"Arthur, is everything okay?" the CFO asked. "I just got a call from Legal. They’re asking why a parrot just emailed them the password to the server."

Arthur looked at Barnaby. Barnaby looked at Arthur.

"Bad bird!" Arthur hissed, lunging for the cage.

"Password is 'Password123'!" Barnaby shouted, flapping his wings. "Also, the CEO is wearing a toupee made of synthetic hair! It’s itchy!"

The office went silent. Heads popped up over cubicle walls. The CEO, Mr. Henderson, walked out of his office, his face a mask of confusion. He touched his head.

"Arthur," Mr. Henderson said slowly. "Why is my bird talking about my hair?"

Arthur scrambled. "It’s... it’s a new marketing strategy! For... uh... transparency! We’re testing a new AI-driven customer service bot! It’s very advanced! It mimics human speech patterns to build rapport!"

Barnaby tilted his head. "Rapport? No. I mimic truth. Also, Arthur, you forgot to take out the trash. It smells like regret and old sushi."

The CFO walked over, arms crossed. "So, let me get this straight. You brought a bird to work, and the bird is leaking trade secrets?"
